items.label: FIGURE B1.1.1
items.title: The composition of the global population has changed since 1990
items.content: The figure consists of two stacked bar charts showing population in millions. Panel a: Population by income group. Categories: High-income (dark blue), Upper-middle-income (light blue), Lower-middle-income (orange), Low-income (red). 1990 data: Low-income 58%, Lower-middle-income 15%, Upper-middle-income 12%, High-income 15%. 2024 data: Low-income 9%, Lower-middle-income 40%, Upper-middle-income 35%, High-income 15%. Panel b: Population by poverty lines. Categories: More than $6.85 (dark grey), Between $2.15 and $6.85 (light blue), Less than $2.15 (dark red). 1990 data: Less than $2.15 38%, Between $2.15 and $6.85 31%, More than $6.85 31%. 2024 data: Less than $2.15 9%, Between $2.15 and $6.85 35%, More than $6.85 56%. Source: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform (version September 2024), https://pip.worldbank.org. Note: Panel a uses changing income groups over time. Poverty rates are reported for the $2.15, $3.65, and $6.85 per person per day poverty lines (expressed in 2017 purchasing power parity dollars).
